title: Choose the visual world for app/index.html
question: The roll assigned the Riso Zine Program. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Riso Zine Program
options.thesis: The whole session as the event's own zine, held in one hand at the booth.
options.viewport: A stapled program spread: duotone room art bleeds full-width, item/object cards ride as punch-hole insert tabs down the right edge, tab nav reads like schedule tracks.
options.risk: Reads twee craft-fair if the ink goes pastel instead of riso-flat and saturated.

raised.raise: Every room spread locks to one shared masthead baseline and scale, category skin or not — borrowed registration discipline.
Only the current room's ink runs full-saturation; every other card sits in the two base tones until it's live — borrowed signal economy.
Unlocking a room tears a perforated edge rather than fading — one committed gesture, not a generic transition.

options.label: Mission Dossier
options.lineage: analog spycraft case files, redacted evidence folders
options.thesis: Every room a case file the team cracks open, the Purge closing in like a redacted deadline.
options.viewport: A case file: a clipped, slightly crooked room photo under a typed brief, evidence-tag cards strung along the bottom, a redaction bar standing in for the countdown.
options.risk: Also the direction most escape-room skins already land on — familiar, but proven for exactly this genre.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: A keyed page: three-digit room address top-left, block-mosaic art filling the cell grid, hidden hint tiers waiting behind a REVEAL flag.
options.viewport: P<room id> index page: numbered rows for items/objects, a HOLD flag on gated rooms.
options.case: Fuses cleanly — rooms already carry numeric card_ids and hints already tier progressively, both map straight onto page-keying and REVEAL; loses narrowly on identification outside broadcast-nostalgic markets.
options.risk: Reads as a UK/Europe-specific broadcast reference this event's Southeast-Asia-leaning audience may not have grown up with.

options.label: Starship Elbow Panel
options.thesis: A wall panel: a thick lilac elbow frames the room art, pill-shaped buttons are the item/object grid, the active pill flashes gold.
options.viewport: Full-bleed elbow frame with a pill-button grid; numeric code cluster stands in for the progress readout.
options.case: Fuses cleanly for tap-target clarity — every pill is an unambiguous button; loses on carrying HKEX-compliance or religious-education episodes, which this dashboard skin reads too sci-fi-specific for.
options.risk: Charming for AWS content, but the same panel dressing a regulatory-filing or scripture episode reads as a costume, not a fit.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Each room a fixed-scale botanical plate tracking one plant's season.
options.case: Fuses poorly — quiet, contemplative comparison-viewing has no path to branching choice or a countdown antagonist.
options.kept: Registration discipline: every plate locked to the same baseline and scale.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller
options.thesis: Depth-as-rank on an emissive void, one bitmap line at a time.
options.case: Fuses poorly — 'nothing ever enclosed by a rule or box' fights the tap-target boundaries a noisy booth needs, and it lands too close to the sci-fi-HUD rut this round was rolled to escape.
options.kept: Signal economy: exactly one accent color reserved for the live/active state.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.thesis: A spectral fringe of color at a cloud's edge, everything else achromatic.
options.case: Fuses poorly — droplet-comparison topology has no branching-room or combine equivalent, and a literal cloud/weather look is the single most obvious reading of an AWS product, exactly the rut this round was rolled to avoid.
options.kept: Color confined to state-transition edges, never filling whole regions.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: One cord-pull turns a flat plane into a gathered, protective volume.
options.case: Fuses poorly — one signature transformation gesture doesn't extend to a shell with rooms, inventory, combine, map, tools, and an admin panel; fashion/textile has no natural foothold with a tech-booth audience.
options.kept: One decisive gesture reveals structure — carried into the assigned direction as the room-unlock tear.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark ops-console HUD this app already ships, executed impeccably instead of replaced.
canonCard.viewport: Near-black ground, glassy surface cards, one accent blue running through timer, buttons, and active states.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other sci-fi-ops dashboard by design.
